answer: Standing is grown, not bought: each identity tends a trellis of signed work records, and only an oasis where records from three separate months interlock in one continuous watering history yields voting weight. New names start parched, holding zero, and anything minted in a single burst stays dry forever, since the ledger refuses to bank two records within the same round. A farm launching k aliases at once must therefore keep each one watered across k overlapping seasons, its capital idling far longer, while a quartz-stamped audit replays the trellis to catch backdated grafts.
